My name is Mama Efe. I was born in Warri in 1951, in a house with a zinc roof that sang when it rained. My father, Papa Okoro, fished on the river every morning, and my mother sold pepper soup at Ogbe market. In 1960, on Independence Day, we walked to the town square and I saw the new flag go up. I started at Saint Mary's School the next year. My best friend was a girl called Tari. We used to race each other home and the loser carried both school bags.
